boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Oakland and Schenley Park destinations on campus-edge corridors, each with a directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: Schenley Park’s active grounds
cards.subtitle: Forbes Avenue & Schenley Drive corridor
cards.notes: Enter from Forbes and Schenley Drive, then choose a marked park facility such as the track, tennis courts, pool, or disc-golf course.
cards.short_summary: A large city park with multiple documented recreation facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Schenley Park at Forbes Avenue and Schenley Drive and identifies courts, a track, pool, fields, and disc golf among its facilities.
cards.access_notes: Use the City’s park listing to identify facilities before heading out; individual amenities may have separate schedules.

cards.title: Phipps’s glasshouse route
cards.subtitle: Schenley Drive corridor, beside Schenley Park
cards.notes: Use 700 Frank Curto Drive for navigation and plan a garden-and-glasshouse visit; bring Pitt ID if seeking the stated student benefit.
cards.short_summary: A documented 15-acre botanical garden and historic glasshouse in Oakland.
cards.evidence_claim: Phipps identifies its Oakland location at One Schenley Park and describes 15 acres with a 14-room glasshouse and 23 gardens.
cards.access_notes: General admission is listed; Pitt students receive free student tickets only during fall and spring semesters, with student ID required.

cards.title: Schenley Plaza’s public seating
cards.subtitle: Fifth Avenue corridor, across from the Cathedral of Learning
cards.notes: Use the plaza as an outdoor pause on Fifth Avenue; its documented seating, gardens, shade area, and carousel make the stop easy to recognize.
cards.short_summary: A restored green space at Schenley Park’s entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitt describes Schenley Plaza across Fifth Avenue from the Cathedral of Learning with outdoor movable seating, gardens, food kiosks, free wireless service, and a carousel.
cards.access_notes: The outdoor plaza is a public green space; carousel rides and food purchases may have separate costs.

cards.title: Carnegie Library Main’s stacks
cards.subtitle: Forbes Avenue corridor, beside Schenley Plaza
cards.notes: Head to the Main branch for a library stop and use the floor directory to orient yourself to the reading rooms, gallery, and collections.
cards.short_summary: The city library’s Main location sits directly on the Forbes corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Carnegie Library’s Main floor directory identifies public collection, reading, gallery, and service areas and lists its operating hours.
cards.source_title: Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh Main Floor Directory
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current calendar before travel; branch services and room access can vary.

cards.title: Carnegie Museum of Art’s cast courts
cards.subtitle: Forbes Avenue corridor at South Craig Street
cards.notes: Enter at the Forbes Avenue Fountain Plaza and look for the Hall of Sculpture or Hall of Architecture; the museum maps several entrances.
cards.short_summary: An Oakland art museum whose building includes major sculpture and architecture spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Carnegie Museum of Art identifies its Forbes Avenue location and describes its Hall of Sculpture, Hall of Architecture, Grand Staircase, and Sculpture Court.
cards.source_title: Carnegie Museum of Art: Our Building
cards.access_notes: Museum galleries require admission; the museum states that its Forum Gallery, store, and café may be visited for free.

cards.title: Natural history galleries on Forbes
cards.subtitle: Forbes Avenue corridor at South Craig Street
cards.notes: Use the shared Carnegie building entrance and choose a gallery stop, such as dinosaurs or a current natural-history exhibition, before buying timed entry.
cards.short_summary: A named natural-history museum with galleries and current exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Carnegie Museums lists the Carnegie Museum of Natural History at 4400 Forbes Avenue and identifies its galleries and current exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Carnegie Museums: Carnegie Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: Timed admission is listed for the shared art and natural-history museums; verify current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Heinz Chapel’s stained-glass stop
cards.subtitle: South Bellefield Avenue corridor between Fifth and Forbes
cards.notes: Approach from South Bellefield and check the chapel’s visitor schedule; use the time to view its documented architecture when it is open.
cards.short_summary: A named interfaith chapel on the campus-edge Bellefield corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Heinz Memorial Chapel states that it is on South Bellefield Avenue between Fifth and Forbes Avenues and is open to all faiths and backgrounds.
cards.source_title: Heinz Memorial Chapel: Directions and Parking
cards.access_notes: The chapel welcomes visitors Monday–Thursday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., but may close for funerals, services, or university events.

cards.title: Soldiers & Sailors’ artifact halls
cards.subtitle: Fifth Avenue corridor at University Place
cards.notes: Start with the Front Hall, then follow the museum’s room-by-room route through military artifacts, photographs, flags, and memorial displays.
cards.short_summary: A Fifth Avenue memorial museum with documented galleries across U.S. conflicts.
cards.evidence_claim: Soldiers & Sailors lists its address as 4141 Fifth Avenue and describes exhibit halls with artifacts and displays from the Civil War through recent conflicts.
cards.source_title: Soldiers & Sailors Memorial Hall & Museum: Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Monday–Saturday hours of 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and paid admission, with listed discounts for college students.

cards.title: Hillman Library’s service desk
cards.subtitle: Forbes Avenue corridor at Schenley Plaza
cards.notes: Enter from Forbes and use the Donald S. Wood Service Desk on the ground floor to get oriented before finding a study or collection area.
cards.short_summary: Pitt’s named main library stop on Forbes Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Pittsburgh Library System lists Hillman Library at 3960 Forbes Avenue and identifies the Donald S. Wood Service Desk on the ground floor.
cards.source_title: University of Pittsburgh Library System: Hillman Library
cards.access_notes: Consult the library’s current hours and visitor policies before arrival.

cards.title: Fountain Plaza’s outdoor sculpture
cards.subtitle: Forbes Avenue corridor at South Craig Street
cards.notes: Pause at the museum’s Forbes Avenue entrance and look over the outdoor works before continuing along the Forbes corridor toward the library and plaza.
cards.short_summary: A named museum entrance plaza with documented outdoor sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: Carnegie Museum of Art identifies Fountain Plaza as its Forbes Avenue entrance and says it contains notable sculptures.
cards.source_title: Carnegie Museum of Art: Our Building
cards.access_notes: This is an exterior entrance plaza; museum entry and galleries have separate admission rules.
